paper_metadata.title: An excellent synergy in yield strength and plasticity of NbTiZrTa0.25Cr0.4 refractory high entropy alloy through the regulation of cooling rates
paper_metadata.journal: International Journal of Refractory Metals and Hard Materials

evidence.quote: a series of NbTiZrTa 0.25 Cr 0.4 refractory high entropy alloys were prepared under a wide range of cooling rates.

the secondary strengthening mechanism (i.e., second phase strengthening associated with Laves phase) was gradually reinforced.

The reinforced second phase strengthening compensated for the weak - ened solution strengthening; as a result, the yield strength first decreased and then increased as the cooling rate decreased without sacrificing the plasticity of the alloys.

evidence.section: 3.2. Evolution of phase components with cooling rates
evidence.quote: Conversely, as the cooling rate decreases, the temporal conditions for the Cr diffusion become favorable. Consequently, Cr atoms are repelled from the BCC lattice structure, affording them opportunities to interact with other elements, such as Zr, ultimately culminating in the formation of Cr 2 Zr Laves phase.
